title: Session details — three versions, pick one

steps.path: Click the tag element in the bottom status bar (was "Tags & note")
steps.headline: Which layout should Session details use? All three share the same top card and Pin to top.
steps.notice: Top card (same in all three): "Session", the name large (click to rename), then "+ Add a note" — or the note itself as plain words, no quotes. Tags on this session are now bigger, filled, with a full-colour edge; other tags are plain grey outlines with only the icon coloured; archived ones are flat grey with no edge, so they never look like "+ New tag".
steps.risk: The sample session has only one tag, so the "On this session" area looks emptier here than with several.

variants.label: One Tags card
variants.summary: One Tags card: this session's tags first, big, then "Add a tag" with the search and the rest underneath.
variants.risk: Applied and available share a card, so the split is shown by size and a small label only.

variants.label: Two cards of pills
variants.summary: "On this session" gets its own card of big pills; "More tags" holds the search, the other tags and + New tag.
variants.risk: One more card, so the page is a little taller.

variants.label: Applied as a list
variants.summary: "On this session" is a list: one row per tag with a Remove button. "More tags" as in B.
variants.risk: Tallest when a session has many tags (one row each).

steps.path: Session details → + Add a note, type, then click a tag (shown in A)
steps.headline: The top card with a note and without one — say if either reads wrong.
steps.notice: The note shows as plain words in the top card, like a project's description; click it to edit. Clicking any tag still opens its edit box inside the tags card.
steps.risk: A long note makes the top card tall and pushes the tags down.

variants.label: Note written
variants.summary: The note as plain words under the name; click to edit. Here a tag's edit box is open too.

variants.label: No note yet
variants.summary: A small dashed "+ Add a note" under the name — the project card's "+ Add a description" recipe.
